brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: Two Full hex bases (piece 0,0,0 and 1,0,0) joined by a joint bolt. A Keyhole hanger (hex-acc-keyhole) sits on slot 3 of the 0,0,0 cell, the mount that hangs the cluster on screws already in the wall. meshClash is clear. I did not verify which face ends up against the wall beyond the part's own placement, so orientation on site should be confirmed.
Five Hook plates (hex-acc-hook, two hooks each, so ten hooks): on 0,0,0 slots 1 and 2, and on 1,0,0 slots 0, 1 and 2. Each is a bolt-on accessory on an outside face.

finish.summary: A two-cell wall rack: two joined full hex bases, one keyhole hanger for wall mounting, and five hook plates giving ten hooks for small hand tools. check_build reports meshClash clear with no rule errors; the only remaining note is optional cap suggestions on four open faces, which I left unfilled.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
